source.title: Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?
source.authors: Rylan Schaeffer; B. Miranda; O. Koyejo

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether downstream task performance changes predictably with model scale, using arithmetic-task performance and alternative metrics rather than held-out pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The paper presents power-law test-loss scaling as background and an illustrative assumption; it does not measure cross-entropy scaling, fit scaling exponents, test extrapolation, or measure compute-optimal allocations. Its own language-model scale results concern arithmetic-task metrics. The BIG-Bench counts and results attributed to prior work are not rows. Vision experiments are included below only as related scale-dependent findings, not as tests of the listed power-law versions.
record.test_reason: The study re-scores fixed InstructGPT/GPT-3 outputs on arithmetic tasks with different metrics and larger test sets. It also re-analyses LaMDA BIG-Bench outputs. Both bear directly on whether downstream performance improves predictably with scale (V6). The per-token cross-entropy power law is only assumed for illustration, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors argue that claimed emergent abilities arise mainly from nonlinear or discontinuous metrics and too-small test sets, not from abrupt changes in model behaviour. They explicitly do not claim that LLMs cannot show emergent abilities.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates fixed model outputs with alternate task metrics and test-set resolutions; it does not reproduce a language-model loss-scaling-law measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Apparent trends vary with evaluation metric, target-string length, and test-set resolution. Vision experiments also vary the deliberately chosen metric or its threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: In vision networks (autoencoders, Omniglot transformers, LeNet), smooth scale trends look abrupt under thresholded or all-correct metrics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Discontinuous metrics can make smooth scale-dependent performance in non-language networks look like sharp capability transitions.

record.problems: The arithmetic results are presented in figures without tabulated values or uncertainty estimates. The paper notes that some model families and their outputs are not publicly available, limiting its meta-analysis to published results. Separate effects for the plotted temperatures are not described in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Predictability from pretraining loss; quantitative extrapolation of downstream performance to unseen scales. Only 4 GPT-3 sizes and qualitative 'smooth/predictable' judgments are given, with no fitted forecast.
Power-law cross-entropy is assumed for illustration, not measured.
Vision models' metrics are scored for emergence, not for power-law form.
Metric dependence of downstream trends is shown, but not dependence of loss exponents or the compute-optimal split on fitting choices.

missing.what: LaMDA BIG-Bench tasks: emergence under Multiple Choice Grade disappears under Brier Score (authors' own re-analysis of released outputs)
Meta-analysis: at most 5 of 39 BIG-Bench metrics show emergence by emergence score; hand-annotated emergence appears under 4 metrics, with >92% under Multiple Choice Grade or Exact String Match

record.verdict_notes: Treated as a T2 test of V6 (it could also be read as T5 against emergence-based exceptions to V6). All language-model evidence is figure-only, based on 4 OpenAI API model sizes, with no uncertainty estimates. 'Predictable' is a qualitative description, not a fitted forecast. The BIG-Bench re-analyses are the authors' own analyses of published outputs, so they are listed as missing rather than excluded as cited results.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
No power law is fitted on small runs and evaluated against larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token split is measured.
The study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count for language-model loss.
Vision experiments change evaluation metrics and do not test whether the same power-law form holds in another modality or training regime.
Tests arithmetic-task performance against model scale, not downstream performance against pretraining loss or other downstream tasks.

The study shows evaluation-metric and test-set-resolution effects on apparent downstream trends, but does not test dependence of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting choices, nor whether loss curves bend away from a power law.

relationships.condition: GPT-3/InstructGPT arithmetic scored with Token Edit Distance, or with accuracy on enlarged test sets
relationships.reason: Authors report smooth, predictable improvement with scale, and above-chance accuracy at all sizes, decaying geometrically with target length as their model predicts (r2, r3, r5, r6). Figure-only and qualitative.
relationships.display_finding: Performance improved smoothly and predictably with scale, with above-chance accuracy at every size and geometric accuracy decay with target length.
